    Oats: steel-cut vs. rolled vs. instant 
     What kind of oats should I buy? 
     Plain oats, steel-cut or rolled. 
     Same grain, cut differently. The packets are where the sugar is. 
     Same grain, processed three ways. Steel-cut are least processed, chewy and slow to cook. Rolled are steamed and flattened, and quick. Instant are pre-cooked and often pre-sweetened. Buy plain oats in any form, and skip flavored packets loaded with sugar. 
     The more an oat is cut, rolled, and pre-cooked, the faster it cooks and the faster it digests, which nudges blood-sugar response up a little — but plain rolled oats are still a clean whole food. The real problem is flavored instant packets, which are mostly added sugar. Plain oats in bulk are one of the cheapest breakfasts there is. Steel-cut are the least processed (chewy, slow to cook, gentlest on blood sugar); rolled/old-fashioned are steamed and flattened (quick, versatile); instant are pre-cooked and often come pre-sweetened. The measured number is the glycemic index: 42 for steel-cut, 55 for rolled and 83 for instant, in one extension comparison.
